items.title: Build a sitemap.xml and keep it current
items.why: A sitemap is the list of pages you want search engines to find, so new posts get found fast.
how: Open /sitemap.xml on your site.
Check it lists your posts, guides and trips.
Make sure it updates by itself when you publish.

items.title: Add a robots.txt that points to the sitemap
items.why: robots.txt tells crawlers where they may go, and a wrong line can hide your whole site.
how: Open /robots.txt.
Check it does not say "Disallow: /" for everyone.
Check it has a Sitemap line with your sitemap address.

items.title: Remove noindex tags from pages that should rank
items.why: A noindex tag tells Google to leave a page out of search, which is a disaster on a page you want found.
how: List pages that carry a noindex tag.
Remove the tag from any page you want in search.
Keep noindex only on thank-you, admin and thin utility pages.

items.title: Add a canonical tag that points at the page itself
items.why: A canonical tag says which address is the main one, so copies do not split your ranking.
how: View the page source and find the canonical link.
It should be the page's own address.
Fix any page that points somewhere else by mistake.

items.title: Enforce HTTPS everywhere
items.why: Browsers warn on plain http and Google prefers secure pages.
how: Type the plain http (not https) version of your home page in the browser.
It should jump to the https version in one step.
Fix any picture or script that still loads over http.

items.title: Every sitemap page answers 200, no 404 or 500
items.why: Pages that error waste crawl time and drop out of search.
how: Open the site health crawl results.
Fix or remove any page that returns an error.
Take dead pages off the sitemap.

items.title: Get your website indexed: submit the sitemap to Google
items.why: A page that is not in Google's index cannot rank at all.
how: Open Search Console, then Sitemaps.
Add /sitemap.xml and send it.
Check the status says Success.

items.title: Pick one host (www or not) and redirect the other
items.why: If both versions load, Google sees two copies of your site.
how: Type the www and non-www address in the browser.
One should redirect to the other in one step.
Use the same version in your sitemap and canonicals.

items.title: Check the Search Console Pages report for why pages are not indexed
items.why: The report names the exact reason, such as crawled but not indexed or duplicate without canonical.
how: Open Search Console, then Pages.
Click each reason under "Why pages aren't indexed".
Fix the biggest group first and press Validate fix.

items.title: Fix broken internal links
items.why: Dead links frustrate visitors and waste the link value you pass between pages.
how: Look at the dead links the daily crawl found.
Point each one at a live page or remove it.
Re-check after a day.

items.title: Redirect every old or deleted address with a 301
items.why: A 301 hands the old page's ranking to the new page instead of throwing it away.
how: Keep a list of addresses you changed or removed.
Add a 301 redirect for each to the closest new page.
Never redirect many pages to the home page.

items.title: Make sure no page is an orphan with zero links in
items.why: A page nothing links to is hard for Google to find and looks unimportant.
how: Check the orphan list from the guide audit.
Link each orphan from a related post or guide.
Add it to a hub page if it fits.

items.title: Remove duplicate pages and duplicate descriptions
items.why: Two pages with the same text compete with each other and neither ranks well.
how: Find pages that share a description or title.
Merge them or rewrite one.
Point the weaker one at the stronger with a canonical or 301.

items.title: Fix or remove thin pages
items.why: Pages with almost no real content drag down how Google sees the whole site.
how: Find pages under about 300 words.
Add real detail, or merge them into a stronger page.
Noindex pages that must exist but have little to say.

items.title: Cut redirect chains to a single jump
items.why: Each extra redirect slows the page and loses a little ranking power.
how: Find links and sitemap entries that redirect twice or more.
Point them straight at the final page.
Use 301 for permanent moves.

items.title: Keep page addresses short, lower case and readable
items.why: Short, clear addresses are easier to read, share and trust.
how: Use lower case letters and hyphens only.
Keep each part under about 60 characters.
Drop filler words and never use underscores.

items.title: Clean up URL slugs
items.why: Messy addresses with numbers and symbols look spammy and are hard to share.
how: Check new posts get a short slug from the title.
Remove dates and ids from slugs.
Do not change a live slug without a 301 redirect.

items.title: Noindex only what you mean to hide
items.why: Old noindex tags from testing are a common reason a good page never ranks.
how: List all pages marked noindex.
Confirm each one is on purpose.
Check the robots.txt does not also block them, or Google never sees the tag.

items.title: Remove mixed content (http items on https pages)
items.why: Insecure pictures or scripts trigger browser warnings and can be blocked.
how: Find items loading over http.
Change the address to https.
Re-test the page.

items.title: Ping Bing and others with IndexNow
items.why: IndexNow tells Bing and other engines the moment a page is new or changed.
how: Set the INDEXNOW_KEY setting.
Check /indexnow-key.txt loads.
New posts then ping automatically.

items.title: Verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools
items.why: Bing feeds several AI assistants, and verified sites get indexing reports.
how: Sign in to Bing Webmaster Tools.
Verify the site and submit the sitemap.
Add the API key so the daily snapshot can read it.

items.title: Run a site crawl every day and read the result
items.why: A daily crawl catches a broken page the day it breaks, not a month later.
how: Check the site health card shows a recent run.
Read the new errors.
Fix errors before warnings.

items.title: Hreflang tags must list the page itself too
items.why: If you have language or country versions, Google ignores the set unless each page lists itself.
how: Open a page that has language versions.
Check its hreflang list includes its own address.
Make each version list all the others.

items.title: Give the 404 page real links and a real 404 status
items.why: A helpful 404 keeps visitors on the site, and a true 404 status stops junk pages being indexed.
how: Open a made-up address on your site.
Check it shows your branded not-found page.
Check it still returns status 404.

items.title: Handle paginated lists with plain crawlable links
items.why: If page 2 and 3 of a list are only reachable by script, their posts may never be found.
how: Use real links for next and previous pages.
Give each page its own title.
Do not noindex page 2 and beyond if it holds unique posts.

items.title: Keep tracking and filter parameters out of the index
items.why: Addresses with ?utm= or ?sort= can create thousands of copies of one page.
how: Make sure canonical tags ignore parameters.
Keep parameter addresses out of the sitemap.
Use one clean address in internal links.

items.title: Look at server logs for crawl waste (advanced)
items.why: Logs show if Google keeps hitting useless addresses instead of your good pages.
how: Export a week of logs from your host.
Count Googlebot hits by address pattern.
Block or fix patterns that waste visits.

items.title: Add a meta title to every page, 15 to 65 characters
items.why: The title is the blue headline in Google and the strongest on-page signal.
how: Put the main topic near the front.
Keep it under about 65 characters so it is not cut off.
Make it read like something a person would click.

items.title: Add internal links between related pages
items.why: Internal links show Google how pages relate and pass ranking power to the pages that matter.
how: Add 3 or more links from each post to related posts, guides and trips.
Link to the money pages from your best posts.
Check there are no orphan pages.

items.title: Give every page its own unique title
items.why: Pages that share a title look like copies and compete in search.
how: Find pages that share a title.
Rewrite one to say what is different.
Add the place or the trip type to tell them apart.

items.title: Add a meta description to every page
items.why: The description is the grey text under the headline and it decides if people click.
how: Write 120 to 160 characters.
Say what the visitor gets.
End with a reason to click.

items.title: Use exactly one H1 per page
items.why: The H1 is the page's main headline and tells Google and screen readers what the page is.
how: Check each page has one H1.
Make the other big headings H2 or H3.
Put the main topic in the H1.

items.title: Add alt text to every meaningful image
items.why: Alt text helps blind visitors and lets Google understand and rank your pictures.
how: Describe what the picture shows in a short phrase.
Skip the words "image of".
Leave alt empty only on pure decoration.

items.title: Write for featured snippets: a direct answer right under the heading
items.why: A clear short answer under a question heading can win the box at the top of Google.
how: Turn a common question into an H2.
Answer it in 40 to 60 words straight away.
Then add detail below.

items.title: Add an FAQ block with real questions
items.why: FAQ blocks win long-tail questions and give AI engines tidy answers to quote.
how: Use questions people really ask.
Answer each in 2 to 3 sentences.
Add FAQ structured data that matches the visible text exactly.

items.title: Fix the heading order (H1, then H2, then H3)
items.why: Skipping heading levels confuses screen readers and makes the outline hard to follow.
how: Read the headings in order.
Do not jump from H2 to H4.
Use headings to outline the page, not to make text bigger.

items.title: Use clear anchor text for internal links
items.why: The words of a link tell Google what the target page is about.
how: Use the topic as the link words.
Avoid "click here".
Vary the wording a little, do not repeat one phrase exactly everywhere.

items.title: Say the main topic in the first 100 words
items.why: The opening lines tell Google and the reader straight away what the page covers.
how: Name the topic in the first paragraph.
Answer the question quickly.
Do not stuff the keyword in again and again.

items.title: Write short sentences and short paragraphs
items.why: Easy text keeps people reading and is easier for AI to quote.
how: Aim for about grade 8 reading level or lower.
Keep paragraphs to 2 or 4 lines.
Use subheadings every few paragraphs.

items.title: Add a TL;DR or key takeaways box at the top
items.why: A quick summary helps readers and gives AI a clean passage to quote.
how: Write 3 to 5 bullet points.
Put them near the top.
Make each bullet a full fact, not a teaser.

items.title: Show the published and updated dates
items.why: Visible dates build trust and tell search engines the page is kept up to date.
how: Show "Published" and "Updated" on every article.
Put both dates in the Article structured data.
Only change "Updated" when the page really changed.

items.title: Show a real author with a short bio
items.why: Search quality guidelines reward content from named people with real experience.
how: Add an author name and photo to each article.
Link the name to a bio page.
Put the author in the Article structured data.

items.title: Have clear About, Contact and policy pages
items.why: These pages show Google and visitors that a real business stands behind the site.
how: Write an About page with real names and history.
Add a Contact page with address and phone.
Link both from the footer on every page.

items.title: Give image files descriptive names
items.why: A file called santorini-sunset.jpg says more than IMG_4821.jpg.
how: Rename the file before upload.
Use lower case and hyphens.
Match the name to what the picture shows.

items.title: Test title wording that earns more clicks
items.why: The same ranking with a better title gets more visitors for free.
how: Pick pages with many views but few clicks.
Rewrite the title with a number, a year or a benefit.
Wait 4 weeks and compare.

items.title: Link out to trusted sources where it helps the reader
items.why: Linking to official sources shows you did your homework and helps AI trust the page.
how: Link to the official tourism board or supplier page.
Open nothing in a new tab by habit.
Skip links to sites that are low quality.

items.title: Read each new post on a phone before it goes out
items.why: Most visitors read on a phone, so a post that looks bad there loses them.
how: Open the post on your phone.
Check text, pictures and buttons fit.
Fix long tables that scroll sideways.

items.title: Refresh pages stuck at positions 8 to 20
items.why: Pages just off page one need only a small push to get real traffic.
how: Find queries at positions 8 to 20 in Search Console.
Improve the matching page: answer more, add detail, fix the title.
Add 2 internal links to it.

items.title: Quality-check AI-written drafts before they publish
items.why: Google rewards helpful content however it is made and demotes unhelpful content made at scale.
how: Keep the quality gate on.
Check facts, names and prices.
Add something only you know to each post.
items.caution: Publishing large amounts of unreviewed AI text is spam under Google policy and can lead to a site-wide drop.

items.title: Match each page to one search intent
items.why: A page that does not match what the searcher wants will not rank, however well written.
how: Search your keyword and look at the top 5 results.
Note if they are guides, lists, trips to book or prices.
Build the page type Google already shows.

items.title: Group keywords into clusters, one page per cluster
items.why: One strong page per topic beats five weak pages that fight each other.
how: List the phrases you want to rank for.
Group phrases that mean the same thing.
Give each group one page and add the extras as sections.

items.title: Make a unique page for each service or product
items.why: A separate page per service lets each one rank for its own searches.
how: List each service, such as cruises, resorts or group trips.
Write one page for each with real detail.
Link them all from a hub page.

items.title: Mine Search Console queries and build pages to match current searches
items.why: Real searches that already show your site tell you exactly which pages to write next.
how: Open Search Console, then Performance, and sort by impressions.
Find queries with no matching page or a weak one.
Write or improve a page for each.

items.title: Find pages competing with each other and pick one primary
items.why: When two pages chase the same search, both rank lower than one strong page would.
how: Find queries where two of your pages both appear.
Choose the best one as the primary page.
Link the others to it with clear anchor text, or merge them.

items.title: Show first-hand experience: real photos, trips and stories
items.why: Experience is the E in E-E-A-T and the hardest thing for copycat sites to fake.
how: Add photos you or your travellers took.
Say who went and when.
Share what surprised them, good and bad.

items.title: Build hub and spoke topic maps
items.why: A strong hub page with spoke posts shows you cover a topic in full, which lifts every page.
how: Choose a big topic as the hub.
List 8 to 15 spoke questions.
Link each spoke to the hub and the hub to each spoke.

items.title: Name real people: advisors, authors and travellers
items.why: Named people with real credentials build trust with both readers and Google.
how: Add advisor names, photos and short bios.
Credit authors on every post.
Link bios to professional profiles.

items.title: Show real testimonials from real customers
items.why: Honest customer words are strong proof and often win a click against bigger rivals.
how: Ask happy travellers for a short quote.
Get permission to use their first name.
Add them to trip pages and the home page.
items.caution: Only use quotes from real customers who agreed. Fake or edited reviews break the law and can get the site penalised.

items.title: Use parent and child pages for a clear structure
items.why: A tidy tree (for example destination, then hotel) shows Google how your topics fit together.
how: Pick a parent page for each topic.
Make child pages for the details.
Link up to the parent and down to the children.

items.title: Prune or merge pages that get no traffic and no value
items.why: Cutting dead weight helps Google focus on your best pages.
how: List pages with no clicks in 12 months.
Improve, merge or remove each one.
Redirect removed pages to the closest match.

items.title: Refresh posts whose traffic is falling
items.why: Old posts lose ground as facts go stale, and a refresh often wins it back.
how: Find posts with falling clicks.
Update facts, prices and pictures.
Change the updated date only after a real edit.

items.title: Plan a seasonal content calendar
items.why: Travel searches peak weeks before a season, so content published early catches the wave.
how: List peak booking months for your trips.
Publish related posts 8 to 12 weeks earlier.
Refresh them every year.

items.title: Write comparison and "X vs Y" pages
items.why: People comparing options are close to booking, and few sites answer them well.
how: Pick two options people compare.
Use a clear table and an honest verdict.
Link each side to its own page.

items.title: Publish original data, surveys and first-hand numbers
items.why: Facts nobody else has get cited by other sites and by AI engines.
how: Collect something you know first-hand, such as booking trends or prices paid.
Publish it with the date and method.
Share it with local and travel writers.

items.title: Prefer improving a good page over writing a new one
items.why: Updating an existing page keeps its history and links.
how: Before writing a new post, search your own site for the topic.
If a page exists, expand it.
Only write new when the intent is different.

items.title: Publish honest "best of" lists with your own picks
items.why: Lists are popular with readers and AI engines when the picks are real.
how: Pick items you know.
Say why each is on the list and who it suits.
Update the list each year.

items.title: Fill topic gaps your rivals cover and you do not
items.why: Every missing subtopic is a search you cannot win.
how: List the headings of the top 3 rival pages.
Mark topics you skip.
Add the missing ones where they help the reader.

items.title: Use programmatic pages only where each has unique value
items.why: Template pages can scale well, but near-identical pages get treated as thin or doorway content.
how: Pick a template where each page has real data of its own.
Add something unique to each page, such as prices or local facts.
Start small and watch indexing before making more.
items.caution: Programmatic pages that differ only by a swapped place name are doorway pages and can bring a penalty. Do not mass produce them.

items.title: Write as long as the topic needs, no longer
items.why: Padding hurts, and so does a thin answer.
how: Cover each question the reader has.
Cut waffle.
Use headings so long pages are easy to scan.

items.title: Add a short video where it helps
items.why: Video keeps people on the page and can show up in video results.
how: Embed a clip of the place or trip.
Add a caption and a text summary.
Use a fast-loading embed.

items.title: Organization / TravelAgency / LocalBusiness on the home page
items.why: This is how engines learn who you are, where you are and how to contact you.
how: Add the business name, address, phone and logo.
Use the TravelAgency or LocalBusiness type.
Keep every detail identical to your Google Business Profile.

items.title: Add valid schema markup (JSON-LD) to every page type
items.why: Structured data tells search engines exactly what a page is, which can unlock rich results.
how: Add the right type to each kind of page.
Test with Google's Rich Results Test.
Fix any block that is not valid JSON.

items.title: Add breadcrumbs, visible and in BreadcrumbList schema
items.why: Breadcrumbs show where a page sits in the site and replace the long address in search results.
how: Show a breadcrumb trail near the top of guides, posts and trips.
Add BreadcrumbList structured data that matches it.
Check the last item is the current page.

items.title: Article / BlogPosting schema with author and dates
items.why: Article markup gives engines the headline, author and dates in a clean form.
how: Add headline, image, author, datePublished and dateModified.
Match them to the visible page.
Use a real author name.

items.title: Add sameAs links to your official profiles
items.why: sameAs links tie your site to your Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and Google profiles, so engines know it is all one business.
how: List the official profile addresses.
Add them as sameAs on the Organization.
Only link accounts you own.

items.title: FAQPage schema that matches the visible questions
items.why: Marked-up questions are easy for engines and AI assistants to read and reuse.
how: Add FAQ markup only where the questions are shown on the page.
Keep answers short and plain text.
Do not mark up ads or hidden text.
items.caution: Google shows FAQ rich results for only a few sites now. Add FAQ markup for machine readers, but do not expect a visual boost.

items.title: Re-test schema in Search Console enhancements after each template change
items.why: A template bug can break markup on thousands of pages at once.
how: Open the Enhancements reports in Search Console.
Look for new errors.
Fix the template and request a re-check.

items.title: TouristTrip / Product / Event schema on trip pages
items.why: Trip markup can show dates and prices in search.
how: Add the trip name, dates, and price range.
Use the real price or leave it out.
Keep dates current.

items.title: Review and rating markup only for real reviews
items.why: Real reviews can earn stars in search, but made-up ones can earn a penalty.
how: Only mark up reviews that customers wrote on your page.
Show the review text on the page.
Do not rate your own business.
items.caution: Self-serving or fake review markup is against Google policy and can remove all your rich results.

items.title: ImageObject: real image with size and description
items.why: Good image markup helps pictures show in image search and Discover.
how: Use a large, real photo (at least 1200 pixels wide).
Add a description.
Avoid SVG or logos as the main image.

items.title: VideoObject schema for embedded videos
items.why: Video markup can earn a video result and a thumbnail in search.
how: Add name, description, thumbnail and upload date.
Match the video on the page.
Test it in the Rich Results Test.

items.title: WebSite schema with the site name
items.why: It tells Google the exact name to show for the site in results.
how: Add WebSite markup on the home page.
Use the short site name.
Keep it matching the title tag.

items.title: Add speakable markup to short answer passages
items.why: Speakable tells voice assistants which part of the page to read out.
how: Pick the summary or answer paragraph.
Mark it with speakable.
Keep it to two or three sentences.
items.caution: Speakable is still in beta and only works for news publishers in some countries. Low priority.

items.title: Use question headings that match how people ask
items.why: Answer engines look for a heading that matches the question and a short answer under it.
how: Turn topics into real questions, such as "When is the best time to visit Lisbon?".
Use them as H2 headings.
Answer in the first sentence under the heading.

items.title: Give a 40 to 60 word direct answer under each question
items.why: This length fits the featured snippet box and is easy for AI to quote.
how: Write the plain answer first.
Count about 40 to 60 words.
Add detail, tips and links after it.

items.title: Use lists and tables for steps, prices and comparisons
items.why: Lists and tables are the format snippets and AI answers pick most often.
how: Use numbered steps for how-to.
Use bullets for options.
Use a table when comparing three or more things.

items.title: Mine People Also Ask boxes for your topics
items.why: People Also Ask shows the exact follow-up questions to answer.
how: Search your main topic in Google.
Copy the People Also Ask questions.
Answer them as short sections or FAQ entries.

items.title: Write answers in natural, spoken phrasing
items.why: Voice assistants read short, plain answers.
how: Read the answer out loud.
Cut jargon.
Keep it one or two sentences long.

items.title: Start topic pages with a clear one-sentence definition
items.why: "X is Y that does Z" sentences are what answer engines quote.
how: Write one plain sentence that defines the topic.
Put it at the top.
Follow with the details.

items.title: Use numbered steps for how-to content
items.why: Steps can win a how-to snippet and are easy for AI to repeat.
how: Number each step.
Start each with a verb.
Keep one action per step.

items.title: Put prices, dates and numbers in plain text
items.why: Answer engines trust specific facts they can read, not facts hidden in pictures.
how: Write the number in the text.
Add the date it was checked.
Do not put key facts only inside images.

items.title: Make sure Bing indexes you, because several AI assistants use Bing
items.why: If Bing cannot find your pages, assistants built on Bing cannot quote them.
how: Verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools.
Submit the sitemap.
Turn on IndexNow.

items.title: Track which queries show your snippet and test new wording
items.why: Seeing which pages hold snippets shows what format works for you.
how: Search your top questions each month.
Note who holds the snippet.
Rewrite your answer shorter and clearer.

items.title: Keep name, address, phone and brand identical everywhere
items.why: Engines build one picture of your business from many sources, and mismatches weaken it.
how: Write down the exact business name, address and phone.
Compare the site, Google profile, socials and directories.
Fix every mismatch.

items.title: Earn mentions of your brand on trusted sites
items.why: Generative engines lean on brands that other sites talk about, with or without a link.
how: Get named in local news, travel blogs and partner pages.
Make it easy: share a short fact sheet.
Track mentions each month.

items.title: Publish original data and quotable facts others will cite
items.why: Engines cite the original source of a number, not the sites that repeat it.
how: Share a fact only you hold.
State the method and date.
Give it a short, quotable sentence.

items.title: Publish an llms.txt file
items.why: llms.txt is a plain guide that points AI tools at your best pages.
how: Open /llms.txt on your site.
Check it lists your key pages with short descriptions.
Keep it updated when you add sections.

items.title: Decide and set the crawl rules for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended
items.why: Blocking AI crawlers keeps you out of their answers, but allowing them lets them use your text, so pick on purpose.
how: Decide: allow for visibility, or block for control.
Add a User-agent group in robots.txt for each bot.
Re-check after changes.
items.caution: Blocking AI bots by mistake removes you from AI answers. Allowing them lets those companies use your text. Pick on purpose.

items.title: Keep visible, honest "updated" dates
items.why: AI answers favour fresh pages, especially for prices, rules and events.
how: Show the last updated date.
Update the page when facts change.
Include dateModified in the markup.

items.title: Add named expert quotes and first-hand stories
items.why: Quotes with a name and role raise trust for people and for AI.
how: Quote an advisor, guide or traveller by name.
Add their role.
Link to their profile if they have one.

items.title: Build strong About us and expert pages
items.why: AI engines check who is behind a site before they trust it.
how: Add names, credentials, years in business and awards.
Link to profiles.
Add a clear "who we help" line.

items.title: Publish llms-full.txt with the full text of key pages
items.why: A full text file lets AI tools read your best content without crawling every page.
how: Open /llms-full.txt.
Check it holds the main pages as plain text.
Keep it under a sensible size.

items.title: Cite authoritative sources for claims
items.why: Linking to official sources shows your facts are checked.
how: Link to the tourism board, government site or supplier.
Name the source in the text.
Check the link still works.

items.title: Structured FAQs on key pages
items.why: Short question and answer pairs are easy for AI to lift.
how: Add 4 to 8 FAQs to guides and trip pages.
Use real traveller questions.
Mark them up to match.

items.title: Keep facts on the site consistent across pages
items.why: Conflicting prices or phone numbers make engines trust none of them.
how: Keep one source for contact details and policies.
Search the site for old numbers.
Fix them all together.

items.title: Take part honestly in Reddit and Quora travel questions
items.why: Forums are heavily cited by AI answers, and helpful, honest replies build real mentions.
how: Answer questions where you have real knowledge.
Say who you are when it matters.
Link only where it truly helps.
items.caution: Posting disguised ads or using fake accounts gets you banned and hurts the brand. Follow each forum's rules.

items.title: Test what AI assistants say about you each month
items.why: You cannot fix what you never check.
how: Ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot 10 questions about your trips and area.
Note if you are named and what they get wrong.
Fix gaps with better pages and profiles.

items.title: Get listed on Wikidata or Wikipedia only if you genuinely qualify
items.why: Knowledge bases feed entity understanding, but they have strict notability rules.
how: Read the notability rules first.
Use independent sources only.
Do not write about yourself without disclosing it.
items.caution: Writing promotional pages about your own business breaks Wikipedia rules and gets removed. Only add what independent sources support.

items.title: Publish helpful videos on YouTube with transcripts
items.why: YouTube is one of the most cited sources in AI answers, and videos also appear in Google.
how: Make short how-to or destination videos.
Write a clear title and description.
Add captions and link to the matching page.

items.title: Keep accurate lastmod dates in the sitemap
items.why: Crawlers use lastmod to decide what to re-read.
how: Check each sitemap entry has a lastmod.
It should change only when content changes.
Do not set every page to today.

items.title: Pick the right main and extra GBP categories and list services
items.why: The main category is a top local ranking factor, and services tell Google what you sell.
how: Look at the main categories your best-ranking rivals use.
Choose the closest as your main one.
Add every service you offer with a short description.

items.title: Complete every part of your Google Business Profile
items.why: A full profile is the biggest local ranking lever you control.
how: Fill in name, address, phone, hours, website and description.
Add the booking or enquiry link.
Check it every quarter.

items.title: Ask every happy customer for a Google review
items.why: Reviews are a top local ranking factor and a strong reason to click.
how: Send a short thank-you with your review link after each trip.
Ask once, politely.
Never offer money or gifts for reviews.
items.caution: Buying reviews, gating them (only asking happy people), or writing your own is against Google rules and can get reviews removed or the profile suspended.

items.title: Keep name, address and phone (NAP) identical everywhere
items.why: Mixed-up details across the web make Google unsure which business is yours.
how: Write down the one correct version.
Compare the site, profile and directories.
Fix every difference, including small ones like Suite or Ste.

items.title: Reply to every review, good or bad
items.why: Replies show you care and give you a chance to use real keywords naturally.
how: Thank people by name.
Answer complaints calmly and offer to fix them.
Reply within a few days.

items.title: Get listed in the main directories and citation sites
items.why: Consistent listings back up your real address and phone.
how: Start with Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp and trade directories.
Use the exact same NAP.
Skip low-quality directory lists.
items.caution: Mass-submitting to hundreds of poor directories is a link scheme and adds risk, not rankings. Use a few quality, relevant ones.

items.title: Earn local backlinks: sponsorships, events and local news
items.why: Links from local sites are strong signals for local search.
how: Sponsor a small local event.
Send local news a story.
Ask each for a link to the relevant page.

items.title: Embed your Google Business Profile map on the site
items.why: A map embed ties your site to the profile and helps local visitors find you.
how: Open your profile on Google Maps and choose Share, then Embed a map.
Copy the embed code.
Add it to the contact page and save the address in the settings.

items.title: Add real photos to your profile regularly
items.why: Fresh, real photos get more views and trust.
how: Add photos of the team, office and trips.
Add new ones every month.
Skip stock photos.

items.title: List products and services on the profile
items.why: The product and service lists feed local search and help match queries.
how: Add each trip type as a service.
Add a short description and link.
Update when you add offers.

items.title: Claim Bing Places and Apple Business Connect
items.why: These feed Bing, Apple Maps, Siri and some AI assistants.
how: Create or claim the listing.
Copy your NAP exactly.
Verify by the method they offer.

items.title: Join the local chamber of commerce and tourism groups
items.why: Memberships bring trusted local links and mentions.
how: Join one or two relevant groups.
Ask for a listing with a link to your site.
Add a "member of" badge only if true.

items.title: Make the address and phone visible as text on the site
items.why: Visible contact details back up your profile and are quoted by assistants.
how: Put address and phone in the footer as text.
Make the phone a tap-to-call link.
Match the schema.

items.title: Study the profiles of the top 3 local rivals
items.why: Rivals that already win show what Google rewards in your area.
how: Search your key local term.
Open the top 3 profiles.
Note their categories, services, photos and review counts, and beat them honestly.

items.title: Keep a steady flow of new reviews
items.why: A few new reviews each month beat a burst and then silence.
how: Aim for a steady number each month.
Add the review link to email signatures.
Track the count monthly.

items.title: Describe your service area honestly
items.why: It stops irrelevant enquiries and helps the right local ones.
how: List the areas you truly serve.
Do not list a city you do not serve.
Match the Google profile service area.
items.caution: Claiming service areas you do not cover is misleading and can lead to a profile suspension.

items.title: Make pages that target nearby cities only when each has unique value
items.why: Pages for nearby towns can catch local searches, but only if each is truly useful.
how: Pick towns where you have real customers or events.
Add local facts, photos, departure info and testimonials for that town.
Skip towns where you have nothing unique to say.
items.caution: Near-copies of one page with a swapped city name are doorway pages. Google can demote or remove them. Each page needs unique, useful content.

items.title: Post updates and offers on your Google profile
items.why: Posts keep the profile fresh and can add a link to your pages.
how: Share a new post or offer weekly or every two weeks.
Add a photo and a link.
Keep it honest.

items.title: Seed and answer the profile Q and A
items.why: Q and A answers show on your profile and help new customers decide.
how: Check for unanswered questions.
Answer them as the owner.
Add the common questions with real answers.

items.title: Keep hours, holiday hours and attributes up to date
items.why: Wrong hours cost customers and reviews.
how: Set holiday hours early.
Add attributes like languages spoken.
Review after any change.

items.title: Check competitor URLs and scan the keywords they rank for
items.why: Rivals show which searches matter in your market and where the gaps are.
how: List 5 rival sites.
Scan which pages and keywords bring them traffic.
Make a better page for each gap you can win.

items.title: Find competitor backlinks and win the same ones
items.why: Sites that link to your rivals are already willing to link to a travel business like you.
how: Use a backlink tool to list sites linking to 3 rivals.
Pick the ones that could also link to you.
Reach out with something worth linking to.

items.title: Ask suppliers and partners to link to your agent page
items.why: Suppliers you already sell for are the easiest and safest links.
how: List your top suppliers.
Ask each to add your agency to their agent or partner list.
Send them a ready paragraph.

items.title: Turn unlinked brand mentions into links
items.why: If someone already wrote about you, a link is an easy ask.
how: Search your brand name in quotes.
Find mentions with no link.
Politely ask them to add one.

items.title: Never buy links or join link exchanges
items.why: Google treats paid and traded links as spam, and the penalty can cost the whole site.
how: Do not pay for links.
Do not trade links on a large scale.
Disavow only if you really have a toxic set.
items.caution: Buying links, link exchanges and private blog networks break Google spam policy and can trigger a manual action.

items.title: Point strong pages at the pages you want to rank
items.why: Your own links cost nothing and move ranking power where you want it.
how: Find your most linked pages.
Link from them to the priority pages.
Use clear anchor text.

items.title: Run a backlink gap report against competitors each quarter
items.why: The gap list is a ready-made to-do list of link targets.
how: List domains that link to two or more rivals but not you.
Sort by relevance.
Work down the list.

items.title: Do digital PR with a real story or data
items.why: A good story can earn links from news and travel sites at once.
how: Make a short data story or travel trend piece.
Pitch it to travel and local writers.
Be honest and give sources.
items.caution: Made-up stats or paid placements dressed as news can backfire and breach link rules.

items.title: Get listed on relevant resource and "useful links" pages
items.why: These pages are made to link out to helpful sites.
how: Search for travel resource pages in your area.
Check your site really fits.
Send a short, polite request.

items.title: Do broken-link building on travel resource pages
items.why: You offer a working page in place of a dead one, which is helpful to the site owner.
how: Find resource pages in your niche with dead links.
Check you have a page that fits.
Email the owner with the broken link and your suggestion.

items.title: Use directories only if they are real, relevant and free of spam
items.why: Good directories help a little, and bad ones can hurt.
how: Skip any directory with obvious ads and no editing.
Prefer trade and local directories.
Never pay for bulk listings.
items.caution: Paying for large directory packages is a classic spam tactic and the links give little value.

items.title: Keep a log of links you earn
items.why: A log shows what works and who to thank.
how: Add each new link with the date and page.
Review every month.
Thank the site owner.

items.title: Keep anchor text natural for outside links
items.why: A set of identical keyword anchors looks like manipulation.
how: Let people link with your brand name and plain words.
Do not ask for exact phrases.
Check your anchor mix twice a year.

items.title: Guest posts only on relevant sites that edit what they run
items.why: A useful article on a relevant site can bring links and readers.
how: Pick sites your customers read.
Pitch an idea that helps their readers.
Link only where it is natural.
items.caution: Mass guest posting for links, or paying for posts with keyword anchors, is a link scheme and can lead to a penalty.

items.title: Set an og:image that is a real picture (not an SVG)
items.why: The share image decides how your link looks on Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp and in AI previews.
how: Add an og:image at 1200 by 630 pixels.
Use JPG or PNG, never SVG.
Test the link in a share debugger.

items.title: Use the same bio, name and link on every profile
items.why: Matching profiles help engines tie all your accounts to one business.
how: Write one short bio.
Paste it on every network.
Link to the same site address.

items.title: Use a link-in-bio page that points to your key pages
items.why: Social visitors need one clear place to go.
how: List the top 5 pages or offers.
Use a tracked link for each.
Update it when campaigns change.

items.title: Tag social links with clean UTM parameters
items.why: Without tags, you cannot tell which posts bring leads.
how: Use the same names for source, medium and campaign every time.
Use lower case.
Never put UTM tags on internal links.

items.title: Repurpose each post into short social posts and clips
items.why: One good article can feed a week of posts at no extra research cost.
how: Pull 3 key points from each post.
Turn them into captions and short clips.
Link back to the post.

items.title: Claim your brand name on the main networks
items.why: Owning the profiles stops others using your name and gives you sameAs links.
how: Check Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and Pinterest.
Claim missing ones.
Add all to the site's sameAs list.

items.title: Optimise YouTube titles, descriptions and chapters
items.why: YouTube is a search engine, and it feeds Google and AI answers.
how: Put the topic in the title.
Write a full description with links.
Add chapters and captions.

items.title: Optimise Pinterest pins for travel searches
items.why: Pins keep sending traffic for months and travel is a top Pinterest topic.
how: Make tall pins with clear text.
Use search words in the title and description.
Link each pin to the matching page.

items.title: Make sharing easy on posts
items.why: Easy sharing helps good content spread.
how: Add share links to the post.
Test them on a phone.
Keep them light and fast.

items.title: Fix the mobile layout
items.why: Google ranks the mobile version first and most visitors use a phone.
how: Make sure the page has a viewport tag.
Open pages on a phone.
Fix text that is too small or buttons too close.

items.title: Pass Core Web Vitals: fast load, stable layout, quick response
items.why: Fast pages rank a little better and convert much better.
how: Check Core Web Vitals in Search Console.
Fix the slowest page types first.
Re-check after a month.

items.title: Compress images
items.why: Large pictures are the number one cause of slow pages.
how: Keep most pictures under about 200 KB.
Use WebP or AVIF where you can.
Resize to the size shown.

items.title: Lazy-load pictures below the fold
items.why: Loading only what is on screen makes the first view faster.
how: Add lazy loading to images lower on the page.
Do not lazy-load the main picture at the top.
Set width and height on every image.

items.title: Avoid full-screen popups that cover content on mobile
items.why: Google demotes pages that hide content behind popups.
how: Use small banners instead of full-screen boxes.
Keep cookie notices compact.
Test on a phone.

items.title: Use caching and a CDN for pages and assets
items.why: A cached page can be served in a few milliseconds from a nearby server.
how: Cache static files for a long time.
Use the host's CDN.
Check the cache headers once.

items.title: Check accessibility: contrast, labels, keyboard use
items.why: Accessible sites reach more people and match what search engines can read.
how: Check text contrast.
Label every form field.
Tab through the page to check the focus order.

items.title: Load fonts quickly and use few of them
items.why: Heavy fonts delay the text people came to read.
how: Use at most two font families.
Use font-display: swap.
Host fonts on your own site.

items.title: Keep page weight and HTML size small
items.why: Heavy pages cost more crawl time and load slower on mobile.
how: Check the page size in browser tools.
Remove unused scripts.
Split very long pages.

items.title: Make phone numbers and buttons easy to tap
items.why: Easier taps mean more calls and enquiries from phone visitors.
how: Use tel: links for phone numbers.
Make buttons at least 44 pixels high.
Keep space between links.

items.title: Verify the site in Search Console
items.why: Search Console is the only place Google tells you how it sees your site.
how: Add the site as a Domain property.
Verify with a DNS record.
Add the service account as a user so reports load in the admin.

items.title: Submit the sitemap in Search Console
items.why: It makes sure Google knows every page you want indexed.
how: Open Sitemaps in Search Console.
Add /sitemap.xml.
Check the status and number of pages found.

items.title: Track conversions: enquiries, calls and bookings
items.why: Traffic is only useful if it turns into leads, so count the leads.
how: Mark form submits and tap-to-call as conversions.
Tag each source.
Review which pages produce leads.

items.title: Set up GA4 with consent handled
items.why: Without analytics you cannot tell which pages bring enquiries.
how: Create a GA4 property and add the measurement id.
Respect cookie consent rules.
Add the property id so the admin can read it.

items.title: Track rankings for your main keywords weekly
items.why: You need a trend line to know if work is paying off.
how: Keep the daily snapshot turned on.
Pick 20 to 50 key phrases.
Look at movement every week.

items.title: Hold a 30-minute monthly SEO review
items.why: A regular habit beats a big push twice a year.
how: Open this checklist, Search Console and your leads.
Note the top 3 wins and 3 problems.
Pick the next 3 fixes.

items.title: Get an alert when traffic or indexing drops
items.why: Catching a drop in days saves months of lost leads.
how: Turn on email alerts in Search Console.
Check the health card weekly.
Act on new errors the same week.

items.title: Watch Bing crawl and index numbers
items.why: Bing powers other search tools, so its view of your site matters too.
how: Add the Bing API key.
Read the daily snapshot.
Investigate crawl errors.

items.title: Note every big site change with a date
items.why: Dates let you link a traffic change to its cause.
how: Keep a simple change log.
Note launches, migrations and template changes.
Look at it when traffic moves.

items.title: Watch Google update announcements
items.why: Big updates can move rankings, and knowing about them stops panic.
how: Follow the Search Central blog.
When rankings jump, check the date against updates.
Do not change much for two weeks.
